info.desc: Debut is the international debut studio album by Icelandic recording artist Björk, released in July 1993 by One Little Indian and Elektra Entertainment. It was produced by Björk and Nellee Hooper. It was Björk's first recording following the dissolution of her previous band, the Sugarcubes. The album departed from the rock style of her previous work and drew from an eclectic variety of styles, including electronic pop, house music, jazz and trip hop. Debut received critical acclaim from British music critics, though American reviews were mixed. It exceeded sales expectations, charting at number two in Iceland, three in the United .

podcast.body: Mentioned as one of Björk's early solo albums that featured an "enormous amount of production work." This style is contrasted with her later, more minimalist approach seen in projects like the collaborative album with Dirty Projectors and *Biophilia*. "Estos discos que tenía un enorme trabajo de producción."

podcast.body: Released in 1993, this album is referred to as her second album, despite her first being in 1977, as it marked her solo debut after departing The Sugarcubes. Its release contributed to her status as a pop culture darling, thanks to her strong female persona, uncategorizable style, and photogenic qualities. "Her second album was called Day View and I know that's confusing because remember she released her first record back in 1977 when she was just 12."

podcast.body: Released in July 1993, this album marked Björk's solo career after leaving the Sugar Cubes. Despite its title, it was not her first album (her 1977 Icelandic album preceded it). It was extremely well received during the Grunge explosion, with Alt-Rock Gen Xers embracing her eclectic styles, including Trip Hop. "debut was extremely well received when it was released in July of 1993, right in the middle of the Grunge explosion."

podcast.body: This album marks the beginning of Björk's solo career and represents her first major musical evolution. It was a perfect example of her transition from a more indie sound to purely electronic music, featuring changes between ballads like "Venus as a Boy" and tracks with powerful rhythmic bases. "es ejemplo perfecto de la transición de la música que iba haciendo más indía a la música más puramente electrónica."

This album, confusingly titled "Debut" despite her earlier 1977 release, marked Björk's solo career launch in July 1993 after she left The Sugarcubes. It was exceptionally well received, released amidst the Grunge explosion, and embraced by open-minded Gen Xers in the alt-rock community, who appreciated her introduction of diverse musical styles like tri-pop and "Björk-ish" sounds. "The debut was extremely well received when it was released in July of 1993, right in the middle of the Grunge explosion."
